claims.text: Exceptional ethanol-oxidation performance is governed by dynamic nanoscale restructuring.
Dynamic restructuring creates a stable, Pt-rich alloy interface with tuned electronic properties.
The Pt-rich alloy interface optimizes adsorption and transformation of ethanol-oxidation intermediates and promotes complete 12-electron oxidation.
The Pt-rich interface suppresses poisoning species, thereby enhancing activity, selectivity, and durability.
Before intervention, the catalyst has an alloy structure with partial surface-composition inhomogeneity and moderate lattice strain.
Reducing-atmosphere thermal annealing will produce a more uniform alloy interface and enhance Pt surface segregation.
Pt surface segregation and local lattice-strain/d-band-center shifts are the structural and electronic mediators of catalytic performance.
Alloying Pt with transition metals can optimize surface electronic structure and improve electrocatalytic performance.
Synergistic effects in multimetallic nanoparticles can facilitate site-to-site electron transfer during alcohol oxidation.
A homogeneous Pt-rich surface adjusts adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates and facilitates electron transfer.
Adjusted adsorption energies reduce the formation or accumulation of carbonaceous and poisoning intermediates.
Reduced poisoning improves ethanol-oxidation selectivity and durability during cyclic operation.
Annealed catalysts will exhibit higher and more stable ethanol-oxidation currents than untreated catalysts.
Annealed catalysts will show less signal decay and products or intermediates consistent with more complete ethanol oxidation.
Untreated Pt-based nanoscale catalysts with poorly defined alloy interfaces deactivate faster because of poisoning and structural degradation.
The proposed mechanism applies at fuel-cell-relevant temperatures and potentials but may diminish when high-temperature sintering dominates.
Extreme pH or aggressive oxidative environments may disrupt the controlled alloy structure and invalidate the mechanism.
The quantitative effect of Pt segregation on the d-band center and intermediate adsorption energies is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes performance to dynamic restructuring during operation, whereas the intervention is described as locking in a uniform, stable interface. It is unclear whether continued restructuring or suppression of restructuring is the proposed beneficial state.
